title: Why most lifters don't train calves (and the solution around it)
summary: NH recounts neglecting calves for years, then failing to grow them because of equipment problems: standing calf machines hurt his lower back, seated machines caused internal knee pain, dumbbell raises hurt his shoulders, donkey raises hurt his back. His experimental solution: heavy explosive 'Toshiki raises' and barbell 'Piana raises' for 6-12 reps plus 100-rep seated EZ-bar calf raises for the stretch, documented in a 'Road to bigger calves' series.

claims.claim: NH ignored calves for years because football and basketball plyometrics and running gave them work, and he was focused on squat, bench and deadlift.
He liked that small calves made his thighs look bigger by contrast.
Many lifters believe calves can't grow and are purely genetic; NH partly understands this but thinks there is a way.
Bodyweight calf raises gave him a big pump but no growth; the stimulus was not enough.
Standing shoulder-pad calf raise machines caused severe lumbar pain even at about 100 lbs, on many machines at many gyms.
Seated calf raise machines gave him good growth for a while but caused pain inside the knee that made locking out on overhead press very painful.
Seated calf machines with non-adjustable pads put all the load directly on top of the knee without the quads elongating to take strain off, which he believes causes knee pain.
Standing calf raises holding heavy dumbbells at his sides hurt his shoulders; he suspects the rotator cuff takes load instead of the traps during heavy static holds.
Donkey calf raises also hurt his lower back.
His upper leg measures 26 inches and his lower leg 16 inches; the discrepancy had become too large to look good.
His calf plan: Toshiki raises (explosive, high-paced, focus on the top extension) and Piana raises (barbell held in front, squeeze at top, slow negative, no bottom stretch).
Do the two heavy calf movements for about 6-12 (or 6-10) reps.
Reserve the stretch for seated calf raises with an EZ bar, done light for 100 reps to an extreme pump.
He admits he has no proof this calf method works and will document it as an experiment, getting stronger on all the movements.
